steps.description: The Chainlink aggregator has not updated the price feed for over 6 hours. The real ETH market price has crashed to $800, but the oracle still reports $2,000. The protocol lacks a staleness check on the updatedAt timestamp.
Attacker deposits 100 ETH as collateral. The lending pool values this at $200,000 using the stale oracle price ($2,000/ETH), when the real market value is only $80,000.

The lending pool queries the price oracle to calculate the maximum borrowing capacity. With 75% LTV and a stale price of $2,000, the attacker can borrow up to $150,000 — nearly double the real collateral value.
Attacker borrows the maximum $150,000 USDC against the inflated collateral valuation. This passes all health checks because the oracle still reports the stale price.

Attacker immediately transfers the borrowed USDC to an external wallet. They have no intention of repaying the loan since the collateral is worth far less than the borrowed amount at real market prices.

When the oracle finally updates to the real price of $800, the position is deeply underwater. The 100 ETH collateral is now worth $80,000 against $150,000 of debt. Even full liquidation cannot recover the borrowed funds, leaving the protocol with $70,000 of bad debt.
